name: Workers IO
long_description:
Workers IO is building simulation environments to catch failures in mission-critical software before they reach production. We run your entire system through millions of simulated production scenarios to verify its correctness and performance properties.

Coding agents can now generate code faster than teams can review it. Meanwhile, software and the infrastructure it runs on keep getting more complex. Tests check a small set of cases in isolation, in environments that are different from production. Some of the most expensive failures only surface when customers encounter them.

We run your entire system unmodified and simulate network faults, disk failures, crashes, and clock drift. We build the fault models for you and check your system’s requirements across millions of scenarios. Every failure we find can be perfectly reproduced.
one_liner: Simulation environments for verifying mission-critical software

launches.title: Workers IO - Deterministic simulation environments to verify mission-critical software
launches.tagline: Run your entire system under millions of simulated production scenarios and verify it never fails.
launches.body:
**Workers IO: Deterministic simulation environments to verify mission-critical systems**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3wW8qNPPswg>

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but verifying what they build still requires significant engineering effort.

The slowest part of engineering now is verification.

Teams need to understand how different parts of a system work together and what happens as they fail and recover. It’s difficult to think through every scenario that could cause a failure, which is why teams often discover these issues in production.

That’s why we’re building[ ](http://workers.io/)Workers IO. We run your entire system, including its dependencies, under millions of simulated production scenarios to verify that it never fails. This allows teams to do years’ worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

Every simulation runs inside a deterministic hypervisor. It uses checkpoints and branches to efficiently explore your system’s state space, verifying different timelines in parallel. Across these timelines, it inject faults, including network delays, disk errors, process failures, and clock skew to verify your system can handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows you to perfectly reproduce scenarios, giving your agents rich context they need to investigate failures and fix them.

<https://youtu.be/TM3ToSRY8GE>

We’re already helping teams whose systems process millions of requests a day, where failures can be catastrophic and verification is becoming a barrier to modernizing their stacks.
